title: 11th Word: Introduction to the Parable and the Sultan's Purpose

questions.question: At the start of the passage, what things are named from creation?
questions.answer: The sun, the moon, the day, the night, the sky, the earth, and the human self.

questions.question: What does the passage say the moon does with the sun?
questions.answer: It comes after it.

questions.question: What does the day do about the sun?
questions.answer: It makes the sun’s brightness clear.

questions.question: What does the night do about the sun?
questions.answer: It covers it.

questions.question: What does the speaker ask the listener to understand a little about?
questions.answer: Why the world exists, why people were created, and the mystery of the prayers.

questions.question: What example does the speaker say to think about?
questions.answer: A short comparison with his own self.

questions.question: In the comparison, what kind of person is introduced first?
questions.answer: A king.

questions.question: What did the king have in his treasures?
questions.answer: Very valuable jewels and other wonderful hidden riches.

questions.question: Besides riches, what abilities did the king have?
questions.answer: Great skill, wide knowledge, and deep learning.

questions.question: Why did the king want to open a display place?
questions.answer: To show his rule, wealth, art, and knowledge.

questions.question: What are the two ways the king wanted beauty and perfection to be seen?
questions.answer: By seeing them himself and by seeing them through other people’s view.

questions.question: What does this tell us about the king?
questions.answer: He wanted his beauty and excellence to be known and seen.

questions.question: What is said about the earth?
questions.answer: It is spread out wide.

questions.question: What is said about the human self?
questions.answer: It was given order and balance.

questions.question: If someone wants to understand the meaning of the world and people, what are they told to do?
questions.answer: Think about the short comparison.

questions.question: What did the king own that was hidden as well as open?
questions.answer: Wonderful treasures.

questions.question: What kinds of knowledge did the king have?
questions.answer: Many amazing sciences and many branches of learning.

questions.question: What do people with beauty and perfection usually want, according to the passage?
questions.answer: They want to see it and show it.

questions.question: What did the king want people to notice in the exhibition?
questions.answer: His power, riches, art, and knowledge.

questions.question: What is one reason the king wanted the exhibition for himself?
questions.answer: To look at his own beauty and perfection.

questions.question: What is the other reason the king wanted the exhibition?
questions.answer: To see those qualities through the view of others.

questions.question: What main idea do these lines teach about the comparison?
questions.answer: The king made a place to make his greatness and beauty known.

questions.question: What opening words in Arabic are followed by an English meaning about Allah?
questions.answer: The words that mean beginning in Allah’s name.

questions.question: How is Allah described in that English meaning?
questions.answer: As Merciful and Compassionate.

questions.question: Name two things the passage swears by from creation.
questions.answer: The sun and the moon.

questions.question: What does the night do that is different from the day?
questions.answer: The night hides, but the day makes things clear.

questions.question: What does the speaker want to explain about the prescribed prayers?
questions.answer: Their mystery or deep meaning.

questions.question: Is the comparison long or short?
questions.answer: It is short.

questions.question: What does the speaker include along with the comparison?
questions.answer: His own self.

questions.question: What shows that the king was not poor or ordinary?
questions.answer: He had many treasures, great skill, and huge knowledge.

questions.question: Why was the king able to set up a display of amazing things?
questions.answer: Because he had riches, art, and knowledge.

questions.question: What did the king want to make visible to people?
questions.answer: The greatness of his kingdom and the wonders of what he had.

questions.question: What are the two “respects” or sides of seeing mentioned at the end?
questions.answer: Seeing with his own eye and seeing through others.

questions.question: What can we infer about the display the king planned?
questions.answer: It was meant to help others recognize how great he was.

questions.question: What shining thing is named first in the passage?
questions.answer: The sun.

questions.question: What shining thing is named after the sun?
questions.answer: The moon.

questions.question: What pair in the passage are opposites in time?
questions.answer: Day and night.

questions.question: What two large parts of creation are also named besides day and night?
questions.answer: The sky and the earth.

questions.question: What inner part of a person is mentioned too?
questions.answer: The self, or nafs.

questions.question: What three big topics is the listener invited to understand a little about?
questions.answer: The purpose of the world, the creation of people, and the reality of the prayers.

questions.question: In the story, what did the king have besides treasure houses?
questions.answer: Hidden wonderful treasures too.

questions.question: What kinds of personal excellence did the king have?
questions.answer: Mastery in arts, broad knowledge, and much learning.

questions.question: Why does the passage say someone with beauty and perfection wants to show it?
questions.answer: Because such a person wants it to be seen as well as known.

questions.question: What did the king prepare so people could see his greatness?
questions.answer: An exhibition with displays.

questions.question: What four things did he want to show in that exhibition?
questions.answer: His rule, his wealth, his art, and his knowledge.

questions.question: How many ways did he want to behold his own beauty and perfection?
questions.answer: Two ways.

questions.question: What are the first verses mostly pointing our minds to?
questions.answer: Signs in creation.

questions.question: Which comes after the sun in the list of signs?
questions.answer: The moon.

questions.question: Which hides the sun’s light from view?
questions.answer: The night.

questions.question: Which makes the sun’s brightness easy to see?
questions.answer: The day.

questions.question: What does the speaker call the puzzle of why the world is here?
questions.answer: A hidden secret or riddle about its purpose.

questions.question: What does the speaker call the puzzle of human creation?
questions.answer: A mystery.

questions.question: What is the listener asked to consider to learn about these things?
questions.answer: A brief comparison.

questions.question: In that comparison, what made the king remarkable?
questions.answer: His great treasures, rare skills, and vast knowledge.

questions.question: Why did the king want to arrange a public showing?
questions.answer: To reveal his greatness and what he possessed.

questions.question: Did the king want only other people to see these things, or also himself?
questions.answer: Also himself.

questions.question: How could the king see his perfection in the second way mentioned?
questions.answer: By looking through other people’s eyes or view.

questions.question: What big lesson comes from the king’s wish to display his treasures and skills?
questions.answer: Great beauty and greatness are meant to be recognized.

questions.question: What groups of created things are mentioned before the comparison begins?
questions.answer: Heavenly things, the earth, and the human self.

questions.question: What does the passage say about the sky?
questions.answer: It has a wonderful structure.

questions.question: What does the passage say about the earth’s shape or spread?
questions.answer: It is laid out broadly.

questions.question: What does the passage say was given to the human self?
questions.answer: Proper order and measure.

questions.question: Who says, “If you want to understand a little…”?
questions.answer: The speaker in the passage.

questions.question: What is one thing the speaker wants the listener to understand about prayers?
questions.answer: Their true meaning.

questions.question: In the example story, what did the king own in large amount?
questions.answer: Treasures and precious jewels.

questions.question: What else did the king own that was not money or jewels?
questions.answer: Great artistic skill and much knowledge.

questions.question: What did the king want to make clear to people by opening an exhibition?
questions.answer: The greatness of his rule and the wonders he had.

questions.question: Why would the king want to look at his own beauty and perfection himself?
questions.answer: Because he wanted to behold them directly.

questions.question: Why would the king also want others to look at them?
questions.answer: So they would be seen from other points of view too.

questions.question: What does the ending of the target passage focus on most?
questions.answer: The king’s purpose in showing his beauty, riches, art, and knowledge.
